full_judgment: 7. Mr. Abdur Rob Chowdhury, learned Counsel, appearing for the respondent submitted that the consequent upon rejection of the application for review on 08.10.1995, the respondent filed the Administrative Tribunal Case on 04.04.1996 which was well within prescribed time of 6(six) months under Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1995; that the authority accepted the review application and passed the order thereon on merit and as such, bar, of limitation, if any, was impliedly condoned by the reviewing authority and the respondent filed the A.T. Case within 6(six) months of the order impugned in the case. The learned Counsel further submitted that the respondent failed to file prayer for review within 3(three) months as required under the provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 is not sustainable since the instant ease has arisen from actions taken under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 and the appellants did not apply the provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 while taking action against the respondent or while disposing of the issue. The learned Counsel further submitted that at the time of rejecting the prayer all other officers in the Ministry except the Secretary were junior to the respondent and all of them were jealous and envious to the respondent for which they were committed to resist the implementation of the orders of the Court in the teeth of the advice of Ministry of Law not to prefer any appeal which will be evident from the fact that in spite of clear regulation that a Government Servant under Suspension, leave including leave on L.P.R., extraordinary leave etc. is entitled to house rent and medical allowances. The appellant deprived the respondent of his due claim.
